name: Executive order of July 1, 1863 setting apart the Crow Creek reservation for the Sioux of the Mississippi
citation: Executive order of July 1, 1863 (1 Kappler 895), under the Act of March 3, 1863, 12 Stat. 819
promises: The Act of March 3, 1863 directed the President to set apart unoccupied land outside any State large enough to give each member of the four Mississippi Sioux bands 80 acres of good agricultural land (57 Ct. Cl. 357, finding XIII).
By the order of July 1, 1863 the President set apart a reserve at Crow Creek, Dakota, on the Missouri River, for the Sioux of the Mississippi (Royce; 57 Ct. Cl. 357).
compensation: None for this reserve. In 1922 the Court of Claims, under a special jurisdictional act, awarded the Mdewakanton and Wahpekute (Santee) $386,597.89 for annuities lost when their treaties were abrogated in 1863, after offsets.
today: The Court of Claims found that the Mdewakanton and Wahpekute held at Fort Snelling were moved to Crow Creek in May 1863, that the reservation proved unsatisfactory, and that they were removed in the spring and summer of 1866 to a new reservation at the mouth of the Niobrara in Nebraska. Royce says the 1868 Fort Laramie treaty later took the Crow Creek tract into the Great Sioux Reservation.

openQuestions: No court, claims-commission or government finding about the Crow Creek reserve itself was found. The Acts of February 16 and March 3, 1863, which took the bands' Minnesota land and annuities, are recorded on cession-1863-03-03-sioux-sisseton-wahpeton-medewakanton-and and the 1858 treaty files.
Deaths at Crow Creek in 1863 and 1864 turned up in secondary search results with differing figures; none was opened and no government admission was found.

treaties.json lists no present-day tribes; the Santee Sioux Nation and Lower Sioux Indian Community (Mdewakanton descendants) and the Crow Creek Sioux Tribe (present occupants of the tract) are named here. Not edited.

Audit 2026-11-08: 57 Ct. Cl. 357 (June 5, 1922) checked: finding XIII (Act of March 3, 1863, 12 Stat. 819, 80 acres each), the July 1, 1863 order (1 Kappler 895), removal to the Niobrara in May and June 1866, and the $386,597.89 recovery. ICC Docket 363 (Lower Sioux, 1975) is a general accounting claim, not a finding about Crow Creek. No change.
